questions.rationale: Correct answer: By that municipal or city waterworks system. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 902.
questions.explanation: Per Rule IX, Sec. 906, PD 1096 requires adequate noise abatement devices but does not specify numerical noise level limits. Those numerical limits are governed by PD 984 (Pollution Control Law) and DENR Administrative Orders on ambient noise standards. The Code creates the obligation; the implementing environmental laws specify the quantitative thresholds.

questions.text: Where should wastewater be discharged when a sanitary sewer main exists?

options.text: To the nearest street sanitary sewer main
To an unlined soak pit without treatment

questions.rationale: Correct answer: To the nearest street sanitary sewer main. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 903.
questions.explanation: Per Rule IX, Sec. 904, rainwater drainage shall NOT discharge to the sanitary sewer system. This prohibition is absolute and unconditional — it applies regardless of sewer capacity, building sprinkler status, or any other factor. Combined sewers cause hydraulic overload (storm events generate 10–100× normal sanitary flow) and contaminate treatment streams. Sections 903 and 904 impose independent obligations.

questions.text: What does PD 1096 RIRR Section 904 say about rainwater drainage?

options.text: It must not discharge to a sanitary sewer
It must always discharge to the sanitary sewer
It replaces the need for storm drainage
It is governed only by room occupancy

questions.rationale: Correct answer: It must not discharge to a sanitary sewer. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 904.
questions.explanation: Per Rule IX, Sec. 902(3), underground sources (deepwells) must comply with PD 1067 (Water Code of the Philippines). PD 1067 governs water rights appropriation — a building owner who sinks a deepwell without appropriate water rights under PD 1067 violates both PD 1067 and PD 1096 simultaneously. RA 9275 governs surface water quality, not groundwater development rights.

questions.text: Which code family governs plumbing installation details such as water piping, wastewater drainage, and venting?
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Revised National Plumbing Code. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 902.
questions.explanation: Per Rule IX, Sec. 905, all buildings with hollow and/or wood construction shall be provided with rat-proofing. This includes concrete hollow block (CHB) buildings where improperly constructed walls leave open joints and cavities that become rodent pathways. The trigger is the construction material type — not occupancy, size, location, or building height.

questions.text: Which item is expressly part of PD 1096 RIRR Section 901 building sanitation requirements?

options.text: A private fire lane in every lot
A fixed air-conditioning system for all rooms

questions.rationale: Correct answer: Adequate and potable water supply. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 901.
questions.explanation: Per Rule IX, Sec. 907, all pipe materials shall conform to the standard specifications of the Bureau of Product Standards (BPS) of the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI). BPS certification covers PVC, uPVC, GI, CPVC, PPR, and cast iron pipes. Installing non-BPS-certified pipes creates a code violation under PD 1096, not merely a quality concern.

questions.text: When a municipal or city waterworks system is available, how should a building intended for human occupancy be served?

options.text: By that municipal or city waterworks system

questions.rationale: Correct answer: By that municipal or city waterworks system. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 902.
questions.explanation: Per Rule IX, Sec. 905, dining rooms for public use that are without artificial ventilation shall be properly screened. This means fly screens on all openings facing outside — windows, doors, and ventilation openings. The public dining context triggers this requirement because food preparation and service in naturally ventilated tropical environments creates fly-borne contamination risk.

questions.text: Where should wastewater be discharged when a sanitary sewer main exists?

options.text: To the nearest street sanitary sewer main
To an unlined soak pit without treatment

questions.rationale: Correct answer: To the nearest street sanitary sewer main. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 903.
questions.explanation: Per Rule II, Sec. 215, inadequate sanitation/plumbing is one of the six categories of defects that render a building dangerous or ruinous. The Building Official may initiate abatement proceedings — ordering repair, vacation, or demolition. This demonstrates that Rule IX compliance is a continuing obligation beyond the Certificate of Occupancy stage, not a one-time construction milestone.

questions.text: What does PD 1096 RIRR Section 904 say about rainwater drainage?

options.text: It must not discharge to a sanitary sewer
It must always discharge to the sanitary sewer
It replaces the need for storm drainage
It is governed only by room occupancy

questions.rationale: Correct answer: It must not discharge to a sanitary sewer. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 904.
questions.explanation: Per Rule IX, Sec. 901, the seven mandatory requirements are: (1) potable water supply; (2) plumbing installation; (3) wastewater treatment/disposal; (4) storm water drainage; (5) pest and vermin control; (6) noise abatement; (7) other health protection measures. A dedicated fire suppression system connected to a municipal water main is not one of the seven. Fire suppression is governed separately under Rule XII, not Rule IX.

questions.text: Which code family governs plumbing installation details such as water piping, wastewater drainage, and venting?
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Revised National Plumbing Code. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 902.
questions.explanation: Per Rule IX, Sec. 903, where no public sewer system is available, wastewater must be treated via: (a) Imhoff tank — a two-compartment sedimentation-digestion tank; (b) septic tank with subsurface absorption field — the most common private solution; or (c) suitable treatment plant meeting DENR effluent standards. All installations must also comply with the Revised National Plumbing Code.

questions.text: Which item is expressly part of PD 1096 RIRR Section 901 building sanitation requirements?

options.text: A private fire lane in every lot
A fixed air-conditioning system for all rooms

questions.rationale: Correct answer: Adequate and potable water supply. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 901.
questions.explanation: Per Rule IX, Sec. 902, when a municipal or city waterworks connection is available, buildings shall connect to it. This is mandatory. The priority hierarchy is: (1) municipal/city waterworks; (2) rainwater harvesting as supplemental source; (3) surface water per RA 9275; (4) underground sources (deepwells) per PD 1067. Connection to the public system is the first and preferred option because public water is regulated and regularly tested.
